Every glyph the keyboard draws around your keys (toolbar tools, the <KeyCap>Shift</KeyCap> and <KeyCap>Enter</KeyCap> keys, the emoji tab strip) is a named icon slot you can replace. Change one icon at a time, or install a pack that redraws the whole set.

The built-in icons, in the keyboard and in the settings app alike, are Google's Material Symbols in their Rounded style, the same family Android itself draws with.

<PhoneFrame caption="The Icons screen: the active pack, and every replaceable slot grouped by where it appears.">
  <Shot id="themes/icons-screen-overview" alt="The Icons screen: the active pack, and every replaceable slot grouped by where it appears." />
</PhoneFrame>

## What you can replace

There are 113 replaceable slots, split into four groups:

| Group | Covers | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | Every toolbar tool's own icon (clipboard, GIF, voice, and so on) | 72 |
| Keys | Shift (off/on/locked), the Caps Lock key, backspace, forward delete, globe, switch keyboard, emoji key, the four arrow-row keys, the Tab key, and Enter in each of its wordings (search, send, go, next, previous, done) | 21 |
| Toolbar chrome | Toolbox, back-to-keys, show-tools, emoji shortcut, close search, incognito badge, power saving badge | 7 |
| Emoji tabs | Search, recent, most used, and one per emoji category | 13 |

The tools group grows on its own as new tools ship, since it's generated from the app's tool list rather than hand-maintained. A pack doesn't have to cover every slot: anything it leaves out keeps the app's built-in icon, so a two-icon pack that only reskins Shift and Enter is a completely normal thing to install.

One thing icon packs deliberately don't touch: the per-key glyphs a language layout author drew into that layout. Those belong to the layout, not to the app's chrome, so swapping icon packs never changes how a layout's own keys look.

**Colour.** An icon that sets no colour of its own (`none`, `currentColor`, or nothing at all) is drawn in the current theme's colour, and picks up that tool's own accent colour if **Colorful tool icons** (under <SettingsPath path="Tools" />) is on. An icon that sets real colours draws exactly as authored and stops following the theme. Most packs should lean on the first behaviour; only go colourful on purpose.

**Vector or picture.** An icon can be an SVG or a picture: PNG, WebP, JPEG or GIF (issue #504). A vector is the better of the two where you have one: it scales to any key height, recolours cleanly and costs a few hundred bytes. A picture is what you have when you drew the icon in anything but a vector editor, and it is the only form a [Gboard theme's own key glyphs](/reference/importing-other-keyboards/#theme-glyphs-and-icon-packs) ever come in. The two behave the same everywhere else in this page, including which slot they fill and whether they follow the theme's colour; a picture counts as "sets no colour of its own" when every visible pixel in it is the same colour, which is what a glyph drawn on a transparent background looks like. A picture may be up to 512 KB and 2048 px on its longest edge; an SVG may be up to 256 KB.

A pack decides which of the two a file is by reading its first bytes, not by its name, so an SVG in a file called `.png` is stored and drawn as the SVG it is.

SVGs are read by a small built-in parser rather than a full SVG engine. It supports paths, basic shapes, and simple color and transform attributes. Gradients, filters, embedded images, and `<use>` references are skipped quietly rather than rejected. A `<!DOCTYPE>` is the one thing that isn't forgiven: that file is refused, dropped from the pack with a note saying so, and the rest of the pack installs around it. See [Icon packs](/development/addon-repos/repo-format/#icon-packs) in the addon repository format for the exact supported subset, the size limits, and why the declaration is refused.

## Replacing a single icon

<SettingsPath path="Appearance / Icons" />

Tap any slot in the list to open its picker. Up to four tabs sit at the top of it:

- **Built-in** is the Material Symbols set, with a search box.
- **Your icons** holds every picture you have added: an SVG, or a PNG, WebP, JPEG or GIF. **Add** opens the file picker, takes several files at once, and puts the first one on the slot.
- **Packs** appears when an installed pack draws this slot, and borrows that one glyph without switching the whole keyboard to the pack.
- **Installed** appears when the phone has an icon pack made for home screen launchers, such as Arcticons. Pick the pack, search its icons, and put any one of them on the slot. A one-colour icon takes the theme's colour like a built-in glyph. The same packs can also dress the app icons of the [app launcher](/tools/app-launcher/#icon-packs).

The picker opens on the tab the slot's current icon came from.

Shift is three separate slots (off, armed, locked) and Enter is one per wording, so "a different picture when caps lock is on" is a matter of filling two slots rather than one. The Caps Lock key a tablet board adds has a slot of its own, apart from the locked Shift: both keys sit on the same board, and each keeps its own face. A key that sends Tab, whether the tablet board's or one you built in the layout editor, draws from the Tab slot.

  ![Picking a replacement for the Shift icon: built-in alternatives, or an SVG of your own.](@assets/screens/themes/icons-slot-picker.webp)
</PhoneFrame>

## Your icons

Every picture you add is kept in **Your icons**, apart from the slots that wear it. Pick a built-in icon for a slot and the picture is still there in the Your icons tab, one tap away. One picture can go on any number of slots, and adding the same file twice keeps one copy. **Use the default** only takes the picture off that slot; it never deletes it.

Touch and hold a picture to rename it, choose how its colours are drawn, or delete it. **Automatic** follows the rule under [What you can replace](#what-you-can-replace): one colour follows the theme, more colours stay. **Keep its own colours** and **Follow the theme** overrule that guess for the one picture. Deleting a picture says which icons wear it and puts them back on their default.

<SettingsPath path="Appearance / Icons / Your icons" /> shows the whole library at full size, for adding many pictures at once and tidying them. **Export as an icon pack** there saves every icon that wears one of your pictures as a `.wmicons` file. It holds up to 200 pictures.

The same tab is in two other places:

- The layout editor's **Icon** row on a key, so a key you built can wear one of your pictures. Exporting the layout carries the pictures inside the file, and importing it on another phone adds them to that phone's Your icons. The small corner hint stays with the built-in set.
- The theme editor's **Key icons** section; see [Key icons in a theme](/themes/editor/#key-icons).

Before Your icons, a picture went into a pack called **My icons**, stored under the one slot it was picked for. The first time the keyboard or the Icons screen opens after the update, every picture in that pack moves into Your icons, including ones a slot had already moved away from, and the pack goes.

**Reset all icons** turns off the active pack and clears every per-slot choice in one tap. It's a full reset, not only the single-icon changes. Installed packs stay on the device, so delete a pack separately if you want it gone.

## Other looks of the same icon

Some icons come in more than one drawing, and their picker opens with an **Other looks** row above the search. The GIF tool is the obvious one: its default is the word GIF inside a box, and **Letters** draws the word on its own. With the built-in icons, the emoji tool and key (a simpler smiley), clipboard (a plain clipboard), settings (a filled gear), voice (a filled microphone, or a sound wave), web search (a magnifier), appearance (a brush), sound & haptics (a speaker), AI writing tools (a robot), hide keyboard (a down arrow) and incognito (hat and glasses) have other looks too. The full list is on the [Icons reference](/reference/settings/icons/#other-looks).

A pack can ship other looks of its own. When the active pack draws a slot, the row offers the pack's looks instead of the built-in ones, and a look you picked carries across packs by name: switch to a pack with its own "Letters" GIF and you get that pack's drawing, switch to one without and you get the pack's ordinary GIF icon.

## Installing a pack

A pack can come from two places, and both end up in the same list of installed packs.

**From an addon repository.** Icon packs are one of the addon types a repository can host. They're capped at 8 MB and, unlike dictionaries or sticker packs, can't be previewed before you install. A set of glyphs is hard to judge from a text description, so it's install-and-look. Installing is a two-step handoff. The pack lands on the device first, then a dialog asks **"Use its icons on the keyboard now?"** with a **Switch to it** button. Declining leaves the pack installed but inactive, so you can come back to it later from the Icons screen without reinstalling.

<PhoneFrame caption="After installing an icon pack from an addon repository, the app asks whether to switch to it.">
  <Shot id="themes/icons-addon-apply-prompt" alt="After installing an icon pack from an addon repository, the app asks whether to switch to it." />
</PhoneFrame>

**Importing a file directly.** You don't need a repository at all: **Import an icon pack** on the Icons screen opens a file picker for any `.wmicons` file, the same format a repository ships. This is the flow for a pack a friend sent you directly rather than one hosted anywhere. Importing switches to the pack immediately, since installing one and not using it isn't usually what you wanted. Pick several files at once and each is installed without switching to any of them, then one message counts them and names any it could not read.

**Several packs at once.** Long-press a pack on the Icons screen to start picking, then tap the others, or use **Select all** in the bar at the bottom. The upload icon there saves the ticked packs in one `.zip` holding a `.wmicons` file per pack, and the trash icon deletes them after asking once. **Import an icon pack** reads that zip back, installing every pack inside it. The built-in icons can't be picked.

Either way, the device holds at most 20 icon packs at once. Inside a pack, an SVG is limited to 256 KB and a picture to 512 KB, and the whole archive to 24 MB.

## Making your own pack

There are two ways to end up with a pack of your own. One suits a pack you're building for yourself. The other suits one you mean to publish.

**Build it in the app.** Put pictures on slots from the per-slot picker described above. When you're happy with it, open **Your icons** on the Icons screen and tap **Export as an icon pack** to save every slot that wears one of your pictures as a real `.wmicons` file. There's no manifest to write by hand, which makes this the fastest way to get a working pack you can keep or hand on.

**Hand-author a manifest for a repository.** A `.wmicons` file is a renamed ZIP: a `pack.json` manifest plus one file per replaced slot, named after the slot id (`icons/tool.clipboard.svg`, `icons/key.shift.png`, and so on). Another look for a slot adds `@` and a name to the slot id, as in `icons/tool.gif@text.svg`; give it one of the app's own look names (`text`, `filled`, `simple`…) and a user who picked that look keeps it when they switch to your pack. The extension in the entry name only says where the slot id ends; what the file *is* comes from its bytes. The full manifest shape, the slot-id table, and the supported SVG subset are documented once, in [Icon packs](/development/addon-repos/repo-format/#icon-packs) under the addon repository format. Follow that spec when you publish a pack into a repository. Export a pack from the app first, as above, and you have a real seed file to edit by hand.

## Options

<SettingsPath path="Appearance / Icons" />

- **Icon pack** picks which installed pack supplies icons for every slot you haven't overridden individually. Default: none (built-in icons).
- **Per-slot overrides** are the icons you've set one at a time from the slot picker. None by default.
- **Import an icon pack** opens a `.wmicons` file someone shared, without going through a repository.
- **Reset all icons** turns off the active pack and drops every per-slot override in one step. Installed packs stay on the device.
- **Other looks** switches one slot to another drawing of the same icon, from the app or from the active pack. None by default.
- **Your icons** is the library of pictures you added (SVG, PNG, WebP, JPEG or GIF), offered as a tab in every icon picker. Empty by default.

When a slot could be filled four different ways, a single icon you picked by hand wins over an active pack, an active pack wins over the glyphs the theme you are wearing brought with it, and those win over the app's own default. Overriding one icon from a pack you've installed sticks even after the pack updates or gets swapped out.

A related setting worth knowing about: <SettingsPath path="Tools" /> has **Colorful tool icons** (on by default), which is what makes a monochrome tool icon (built-in or from a pack) pick up that tool's own accent colour instead of a flat theme colour.

## Details & edge cases

- **Deleting a pack cleans up after itself.** Along with the pack's own files, deleting it drops any per-slot override pinned to it, so those slots go back to the built-in icon right away rather than pointing at something that no longer exists. Installing a different pack under the same id later doesn't bring the old per-slot choices back. You'd pick them again from the slot picker.
- **Deleting the active pack turns off the "active pack" setting** as well as removing it from the list. Any slot that was relying on it, and wasn't separately overridden, reverts to the built-in icon.
- **No build differences.** Icon packs work the same way in every build; nothing here is limited to one.
- **Icon packs travel with backups.** They're one of the sections you can choose to include in a full settings export (off by default, since the SVGs add to the file size), so a restore on another phone can bring your custom icons along too. Your icons rides in the same section.
- **Replacing a slot's icon replaces its file.** Put a PNG on a slot that held an SVG and the SVG is removed, so the slot never has two files and an export never carries the one you replaced.
- **A pack's own `slots` list is advisory, not authoritative.** The app looks at what's actually inside the archive and keeps anything that matches a slot it recognizes, so a pack assembled by hand still installs correctly even if its manifest is out of date.
